two_axes.rule_en: These are two independent axes, not one spectrum. A casual sentence can be Sanskrit-influenced and a formal one can be Urdu-influenced. Any item that treats them as a single line from low to high is wrong.

framing_rule.en: No form is described as pure, impure, corrupted, broken, proper, real, better or worse than any other. धन्यवाद and शुक्रिया are both fully correct Hindi, chosen by situation. The axes are never ranked against each other.
framing_rule.enforced_by: A banned-phrase scan runs over every string in the module before it ships, so the rule cannot lapse quietly at item thirty.

debt_note_en: This module names what the previous fourteen have been doing without saying so. Module 13's pairs block found that the Sanskrit side takes the institutions and the compounds while the other side keeps the conversation; Module 12 found that a single message can hold क्षमा and माफ़ी three lines apart. Both findings are axis-2 observations made before axis 2 had a name.

review_flags: Level 10 makes a claim about where Hinglish jars, and that claim varies enormously by region, age, city and family. The item is written to say so rather than to state a rule, because a rule here would be wrong for a large share of learners.

Every practice item asks the learner to pick a rendering for an audience. The correct answer must not be the most formal option every time, or the module will teach that formality is always safer — which is the opposite of what it is for.
The five situations and four tendencies are fixed vocabularies. Any register_tag outside those lists, or any item whose axis does not match its tags, should fail validation.
